rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Quraysh have decided to deny the Qur’an and Messenger, God will make a final decision in response.
rows.anchor: if they have made a final decision, then the Almighty too will make a final decision.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives a nation respite while it hesitates, but when it resolves to kill or expel its messenger, He protects the messenger and companions and destroys the nation.
rows.anchor: takes the messenger and his companions in His refuge and destroys the rest of the nation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secret whispers refer to Quraysh plotting at dār al-nadwah to kill or expel the Prophet from Mecca.
rows.anchor: secret whisperings which the Quraysh were doing in dār al-nadwah viz a viz killing or turning out the Prophet (sws) from Makkah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their conspiracies, and angels record every deed; when Quraysh decide against the Messenger, God’s judgment will appear and their plans will fail.
rows.anchor: His angels are keeping a written record of each and every deed of theirs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says hypothetically that if God had children, he would be the first to worship them.
rows.anchor: if it is proven that God does have children then, he – the Prophet (sws) – would be the first to worship them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration returns to the sūrah’s opening refutation of the angels’ divinity.
rows.anchor: referring to the discussion found in the opening verses of the sūrah viz a viz the refutation of divinity of the angels

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created, owns, and rules the universe; He needs no son, daughter, helper, or partner.
rows.anchor: He alone is the creator of all these things and He alone is the master of this universe and solely rules it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above the unsupported attributions made by the idolaters and is independent of offspring, helpers, and partners.
rows.anchor: neither is He in need of a son nor daughter. He also does not require a helper or a partner.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to leave the rejecters to their excuses and frivolous talk until the threatened Day, when their alleged gods will not help them.
rows.anchor: let them make whatever excuses they want to and let them indulge their frivolous talk until they encounter the Day they are being threatened with.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered harmony of heaven and earth indicates that one sustaining will governs them; multiple wills would have destroyed them.
rows.anchor: The harmony found between the heavens and the earth shows that they are working under the will of a single powerful and sustaining being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s wisdom and knowledge leave no basis for the idolaters’ confidence in intercession, which contradicts both attributes.
rows.anchor: Thus the false belief of intercession on the basis of which the Idolaters have become fearless of the Hereafter has no foundation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of God as blessed conveys both His greatness and His goodness and graciousness.
rows.anchor: encompasses in it the aspect of God’s greatness as well as He being an embodiment of good and graciousness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s greatness and graciousness mean that people should fear and hope in Him alone; His sovereignty bars interference, while His mercy governs His treatment.
rows.anchor: only He should be feared and all hopes should be pinned only in Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the Hour; the Prophets’ inability to name its time does not mean it will not come.
rows.anchor: the knowledge of the hour of Judgement is only with God; if prophets of God are not able to tell its time of arrival

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is certain, everyone will return to God alone, and people should expect no help from another being.
rows.anchor: if prophets of God are not able to tell its time of arrival, then it does not mean that it will not come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters wrongly expect their alleged deities to protect them and secure release through intercession; those invoked besides God have no such authority, and judgment belongs to God.
rows.anchor: The verse says that those who they invoke other than God have no authority to intercede.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Mu’min confirms that God judges justly and the beings invoked besides Him cannot judge anything.
rows.anchor: God will decide with absolute justice and those who they invoke other than God will not judge any thing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is severed: no one intercedes, while those God permits instead bear truthful witness to what they know.
rows.anchor: no one will have the authority to intercede; however, those whom the Almighty permits will bear witness to the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah Ṭāhā says intercession is useful only for someone God permits and about whom He allows speech.
rows.anchor: on that day, intercession will be of no avail to anyone except for whom God grants permission

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Naba’ likewise says that speakers must have the Merciful’s permission and speak the truth.
rows.anchor: they will not speak unless whom the most Gracious allows and he shall speak the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus testifies only to the period he witnessed among his people; he did not know what happened after his departure, and God alone witnessed it.
rows.anchor: I was a witness to them as long as I remained among them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters admit that God created them, making it astonishing that they then imagine other beings can intercede and release people from God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: if they are asked about their creator; their answer in all cases will be God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony clause coordinates with the truth clause in 43:86; 43:87 is a parenthetical qualification, so the linked clauses remain together.
rows.anchor: a parenthetical one to express a modification ( istidrāk). Thus the conjugate and conjugated sentences were not distanced from one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses’ truthful testimony is that the rejecters themselves are responsible for refusing to believe.
rows.anchor: they themselves are to be blamed for not embracing faith; they were not prepared to take this step.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an depicts angels disavowing the idolaters’ claim that they worshipped them, saying the people instead worshipped jinn and followed them.
rows.anchor: in fact, they have been worshipping the jinn and a majority of them profess faith in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus denies telling people to worship him and his mother, saying he had no authority to make such a claim and God knew the truth.
rows.anchor: Jesus son of Mary, did you tell people: ‘Regard me and my mother as gods except God?’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Aḥqāf says invoked beings cannot answer their worshippers and will become their enemies and disown their worship at the gathering.
rows.anchor: they will declare themselves their enemies and will disown their worship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the rejecters insist on seeing their fate, the Prophet should leave and ignore them as Abraham did with his father.
rows.anchor: leave them alone and ignore them the way Abraham (sws) had done with his father.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word salām here means good-bye.
rows.anchor: The word ﺳﻠٰﻢٌ connotes “good-bye.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fate they await is near; they will soon see it.
rows.anchor: the fate which they await is not far off; they shall soon witness it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taysīr means making something suitable for its purpose and firm and sound in every respect.
rows.anchor: means to make something appropriate and suitable for a purpose and to make it firm and sound in all aspects.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the sense with preparing a horse for riding by equipping it, and applies the analogy to furnishing the Qur’an for education and reminder.
rows.anchor: to make a horse ready for riding by adorning it with a bridle, saddle, stirrups and other relevant things.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the view that the verse calls the Qur’an merely easy and bland: its ease serves teaching and reminder, while its comprehensive subject matter includes intricate matters.
rows.anchor: this verse to mean that the Qur’ ān is a very easy and bland book have not been able to grasp the essence of the word.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an communicates intricate matters of wisdom to hearts through majestic, inimitable styles, though those matters require deep deliberation.
rows.anchor: it has adopted such majestic styles which cannot be emulated by anyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi refers readers to his discussion of 19:97 and says he will revisit the issue in his commentary on Sūrah al-Qamar.
rows.anchor: the explanation of verse 97 of S ūrah Maryam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s tongue is the pure, unadulterated Quraysh dialect, the best archetype of eloquent Arabic; the Prophet exemplifies it.
rows.anchor: the pure and unadulterated language of the Quraysh which was the best archetype of eloquent Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation in the Prophet’s exemplary Quraysh Arabic conclusively communicated the truth; failure to understand it is the hearers’ fault, not the Book’s or Prophet’s.
rows.anchor: to conclusively communicate the truth to the Quraysh, the Almighty has revealed this Book in the language of the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an aims to remind people of truths granted by intellect and nature, lessons in themselves and the world, and guidance from earlier Prophets, especially Abraham.
rows.anchor: express the purpose of the revelation of the Qur’ ān in a very elaborate and thorough manner: to receive reminder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose also warns that those who refuse reminder should expect the fate of rebellious people, which their own history recalls.
rows.anchor: if they are not prepared to be reminded, then they should get ready to meet the fate destined by God for such rebellious people.
